types.name: data
types.description:
The data used initiate a payment in a provider when a payment
session is created.

children.name: data
children.description: Data is a combination of the input from the user and what is stored in the database for the associated model.

children.name: context
children.description: The context for this payment operation. The data is guaranteed to be validated and not directly provided by the user.

children.name: account_holder
children.description: The account holder information, if available for the payment provider.

children.name: customer
children.description: The customer information from Medusa.

children.name: idempotency_key
children.description: Idempotency key for the request, if the payment provider supports it. It will be ignored otherwise.

children.name: amount
children.description: The amount to be authorized.

children.name: currency_code
children.description: The ISO 3 character currency code.

children.name: data
children.description: The unstructured data returned from the payment provider. The content will vary between providers.

children.name: id
children.description: The ID of the payment session in the payment provider.

children.name: status
children.description: The status of the payment session, which will be stored in the payment session's `status` field.

blocks.html:
This method is used when retrieving an account holder in Medusa, allowing you to retrieve
the equivalent account in the third-party payment provider. An account holder is useful to
later save payment methods, such as credit cards, for a customer in the
third-party payment provider using the [savePaymentMethod](/references/types/interfaces/types.IPaymentProvider#savepaymentmethod) method.
This is available starting from [Medusa v2.11.0](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/releases/tag/v2.11.0).

types.name: data
types.description: Input data including the details of the account holder to retrieve.

children.name: data
children.description: Data is a combination of the input from the user and what is stored in the database for the associated model.

children.name: context
children.description: The context for this payment operation. The data is guaranteed to be validated and not directly provided by the user.

children.name: account_holder
children.description: The account holder information, if available for the payment provider.

children.name: customer
children.description: The customer information from Medusa.

children.name: idempotency_key
children.description: Idempotency key for the request, if the payment provider supports it. It will be ignored otherwise.

children.name: id
children.description: The ID of the account holder to retrieve.

types.name: Promise
types.description: The retrieved account holder. If an error occurs, throw it.

children.name: data
children.description: The unstructured data returned from the payment provider. The content will vary between providers.

children.name: id
children.description: The ID of the account holder in the payment provider.

blocks.html:
This method is used when creating an account holder in Medusa, allowing you to create
the equivalent account in the third-party payment provider. An account holder is useful to
later save payment methods, such as credit cards, for a customer in the
third-party payment provider using the [savePaymentMethod](/references/types/interfaces/types.IPaymentProvider#savepaymentmethod) method.

The returned data will be stored in the account holder created in Medusa. For example,
the returned `id` property will be stored in the account holder's `external_id` property.

Medusa creates an account holder when a payment session initialized for a registered customer.
This is available starting from [Medusa v2.5.0](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/releases/tag/v2.5.0).

types.name: data
types.description: Input data including the details of the account holder to create.

children.name: data
children.description: Data is a combination of the input from the user and what is stored in the database for the associated model.

children.name: context
children.description: The context of creating the account holder.

children.name: account_holder
children.description: The account holder information, if available for the payment provider.

children.name: idempotency_key
children.description: Idempotency key for the request, if the payment provider supports it. It will be ignored otherwise.

children.name: customer
children.description: The account holder's associated customer details.

types.name: Promise
types.description: The result of creating the account holder. If an error occurs, throw it.

children.name: data
children.description: The unstructured data returned from the payment provider. The content will vary between providers.

children.name: id
children.description:
The ID of the account holder in the payment provider.
This is stored in Medusa's account holder in the `external_id` property.

blocks.html:
This method is used when updating an account holder in Medusa, allowing you to update
the equivalent account in the third-party payment provider.

The returned data will be stored in the account holder created in Medusa. For example,
the returned `id` property will be stored in the account holder's `external_id` property.
This is available starting from [Medusa v2.5.1](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/releases/tag/v2.5.1).

blocks.html:
This method is used to retrieve the list of saved payment methods for an account holder
in the third-party payment provider. A payment provider that supports saving payment methods
must implement this method.
This is available starting from [Medusa v2.5.0](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/releases/tag/v2.5.0).

types.description: Input data including the details of the account holder to list payment methods for.

children.description: The account holder information, if available for the payment provider.

children.name: customer
children.description: The customer information from Medusa.

children.name: idempotency_key
children.description: Idempotency key for the request, if the payment provider supports it. It will be ignored otherwise.

This method is used to save a customer's payment method, such as a credit card, in the
third-party payment provider. A payment provider that supports saving payment methods
must implement this method.
This is available starting from [Medusa v2.5.0](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/releases/tag/v2.5.0).
